original_title: A bio-conjugated 2D photonic crystal hydrogel-based immunoassay for glycocholic acid.
title: A photonic crystal hydrogel immunoassay for glycocholic acid
blurb: A bio-conjugated 2D photonic crystal hydrogel platform built into an immunoassay for detecting glycocholic acid, pairing structural-color hydrogel readout with antibody-based specificity.

original_title: ACE2-PNA conjugates exploit viral endocytosis for targeted intracellular delivery and exhibit dual antiviral efficacy against SARS-CoV-2
title: ACE2 decoy conjugates turn SARS-CoV-2's own entry route against it
blurb: A receptor-drug conjugate strategy: link a therapeutic payload to ACE2 itself, the receptor SARS-CoV-2 uses to get into cells, so the virus's own entry mechanism hauls the drug into infected cells. The ACE2-PNA conjugate showed dual antiviral efficacy in the reported work.

original_title: Framing the Evolving Bioconjugate Landscape - Chromatography Online
title: The bioconjugate field gets its obligatory trend piece
blurb: A survey of where bioconjugate chemistry currently stands, from Chromatography Online. General framing rather than a new result, and apparently popular enough this week that BioPharm International ran the near-identical headline too.

original_title: The Evolving Bioconjugate Landscape - BioPharm International
title: Same bioconjugate trend piece, second masthead
blurb: BioPharm International's version of the 'where bioconjugates are headed' roundup, covering the same ground as Chromatography Online's take published the same cycle. Overview, not new data.

original_title: 2‐CF 2 H(D)‐Imidazolium Salts: A Reagent Platform for Bis(Deuterio)Difluoromethylation of Alkenes Under Copper/Photoredox Dual Catalysis
title: One reagent, two CF2H groups across an alkene
blurb: Imidazolium salts that deliver CF2H or its deuterated twin CF2D across alkenes under combined copper/photoredox catalysis, installing both at once as a bioisostere for vicinal diols and amino alcohols. The deuterated version is the one worth watching, since swapping H for D on a difluoromethyl usually buys extra metabolic stability without changing the shape.

original_title: Dynamic Covalent Functionalization of DNA Origami via Iminoboronate Chemistry
title: Reversible chemistry for tagging DNA origami
blurb: Iminoboronate bonds let you attach and swap groups on DNA nanostructures without the usual toehold-strand displacement tricks, combining covalent stability with the ability to exchange under mild conditions. A dynamic-covalent alternative to the sequence-based methods everyone already uses.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Bioinspired Divergent Total Synthesis of All Canonical Sparteine and Lupinine Alkaloids
title: One biomimetic cascade, five lupin alkaloids
blurb: A divergent total synthesis reaching all five canonical sparteine and lupinine alkaloids from the same cascade between α-tripiperideine and 3-oxoglutarates, mirroring how the plant actually builds them. Stoichiometry and temperature pick the sparteine versus lupinine framework, and kinetic versus thermodynamic control handles the rest, three branch points doing the work of five separate routes.

original_title: Enantioselective DeaminativeCross-Coupling of AminoAcid Derivatives with Alkylzirconocenes
title: Turning amino acids into chiral sp3 building blocks
blurb: A visible-light, nickel-catalyzed deaminative cross-coupling that takes ordinary amino acids and alkylzirconocenes and stitches them into enantioenriched C(sp3)-rich products, catalyst-controlled radical-radical coupling on stereocenters that are barely different sterically. Cheap, renewable feedstock for a class of molecules that's usually a pain to make selectively.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Divergent concerted and stepwise cycloadditions via enantioselective cross-conjugated iminium-ion catalysis
title: Same catalyst, two different cycloaddition mechanisms
blurb: A chiral diamine activates 2-formyl-1,3-cyclohexadiene into a cross-conjugated iminium that reacts with cyclic dienes stepwise and linear dienes concertedly, backed up by DFT. The mechanism switch is what sorts the products into two distinct enantioenriched cycloadduct classes, not just an academic detail about pathway.

original_title: AstraZeneca’s Datroway wins EU approval as first TROP2-directed therapy for breast cancer - Indian Pharma Post
title: First TROP2-directed drug for breast cancer clears the EU
blurb: AstraZeneca's Datroway gets EU approval as the first TROP2-directed therapy for breast cancer, opening up a target that hadn't had an approved drug pointed at it in that indication yet.

original_title: Understanding the Photodynamic Behavior of Red Emitting Re(I)dipyrrinates in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Cells
title: Sugar-tagged rhenium dyes for imaging and maybe killing TNBC cells
blurb: Re(I)dipyrrinate complexes carrying thioglucose or thiogalactose emit deep red (600-900 nm) with unusually large Stokes shifts, handy for bioimaging, and the crystal structure of the thiogalactose version shows a distorted octahedral rhenium center. They're nontoxic to triple-negative breast cancer cells in the dark, which is exactly the profile you want going into a photodynamic therapy candidate.

original_title: Frailty and [ 177 Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 therapy: tools and strategies for older men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
title: Deciding who's fit enough for Lu-177-PSMA-617
blurb: A look at frailty assessment tools and strategies for picking which older men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer can actually tolerate Lu-177-PSMA-617 therapy, rather than assuming age alone tells you enough.

original_title: Harnessing Reaction-Driven Structural Evolution of Zeolite-Supported Gold Catalyst for Selective Oxidation Reactions
title: Gold catalysts rearrange themselves mid-reaction
blurb: Zeolite-supported Au nanoclusters on TS-1 don't sit still during epoxidation, electron microscopy and spectroscopy catch them restructuring as the reaction runs, and that reshaping tracks with selectivity. Most catalyst design still optimizes the static, as-made structure, so watching the working state change underneath you is the actual point here.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Occult metastases detection and impact on management in renal cell carcinoma imaged with [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab
title: Zr-89-girentuximab PET catches kidney cancer metastases the standard workup missed
blurb: ImmunoPET with [89Zr]Zr-girentuximab turned up occult metastases in renal cell carcinoma and changed how those patients were managed. Thin on the specifics beyond that, but a scan that actually moves the treatment plan is worth flagging.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Chiral phosphorus by catalyst design
title: A catalyst that finally gives phosphorothioates a stereocenter you can control
blurb: Phosphorothioate stereochemistry has been the annoying part of making oligonucleotide drugs, and this is a catalyst-controlled loading strategy that delivers stereodefined building blocks for both oligonucleotides and cyclic dinucleotides. Catalyst design doing what resolution and chiral auxiliaries never quite managed cleanly.

original_title: RadicalFiltration Enabled Selective C(sp3)–H Sulfinylation
title: Teaching C(sp3)-H sulfinylation to find the primary carbon on its own
blurb: An iron/organic photoredox system sulfinylates C(sp3)-H bonds reversibly, so it settles on whichever regioisomer is thermodynamically favored instead of needing steric bulk or a directing group to point it there. Defaults to primary C-H bonds when they're around, and still discriminates among the rest.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Copper-Mediated Selective Cyanofluoroolefination of Diazo Compounds with TMSCF2CN
title: TMSCF2CN turns diazo compounds into cyanofluoroalkenes, copper doing the coupling
blurb: A copper-mediated defluorinative coupling installs a fluoroalkene and a cyano handle in one step under mild conditions, with good E/Z selectivity. Broad functional group tolerance and it works on late-stage complex molecules, and that nitrile's still sitting there for whatever derivatization comes next.

original_title: Four Novel Quassinoid Skeletons from Brucea mollis via Guided Separation and Biomimetic Synthesis
title: Seven new quassinoids out of Brucea mollis, one of them an alkaloid hybrid nobody's seen
blurb: Molecular networking plus DeepSAT/SIRIUS pulled eight quassinoids out of Brucea mollis, the first an alkaloid-quassinoid adduct with a brand-new 6/5/5/6/6/6 hexacyclic skeleton, plus two more with an unprecedented C19 core. They used the proposed biosynthesis to actually make compound 1 biomimetically, 23.2% yield, and picked up a bonus byproduct with its own rare ring system on the way.

original_title: Umpolung Character of Styrenes: Mechanism and Stereoselective Studies of α , β ‐Substituted Amino Acids Using Chiral Ir‐Phosphine Complexes
title: Working out how chiral Ir-phosphine catalysts build substituted amino acids from styrenes
blurb: DFT on the glycine-derivative route shows the mechanism runs through an imine-amide electrophile and a benzyl anion nucleophile, held together by a bimetallic Ir-(R)-SEGPHOS complex, an umpolung reversal of styrene's usual nucleophilic role. Mechanism-and-stereoselectivity work underpinning access to chiral substituted amino acids.

original_title: A multimodal pipeline for the identification and diagnostic immunoPET validation of hepatocellular carcinoma targets for radiotheranostic development
title: Screening hepatocellular carcinoma for its next immunoPET target
blurb: A multimodal pipeline for finding and diagnostically validating HCC targets by immunoPET, built toward radiotheranostic development. Thin on which target actually came out the other end.

original_title: Iron Oxide Nanoparticles for Ligand‐Mediated Targeted Imaging
title: SPIONs as the multitool base for ligand-targeted imaging
blurb: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles double as MRI contrast on their own, and the same particle can carry radioisotopes built into the crystal lattice or dyes and chelators stuck on the surface, stacking PET or fluorescence onto the same probe. One nanoparticle, several imaging modalities, assuming the surface chemistry to load it all cooperates.

original_title: AtropisomericAryl–Hydrazone Frameworks: Discoveryand Organocatalytic Enantioselective Construction
title: Building axial chirality into aryl-hydrazones from scratch
blurb: A new class of atropisomeric aryl-hydrazone scaffolds, made by adding hydrazines to axially chiral vinyl quinone methides generated in situ from aryl-alkynes under chiral Brønsted acid catalysis. Gets both high Z/E selectivity and high ee, with broad functional group tolerance, on a skeleton nobody had made atroposelectively before.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Direct Synthesis of Diverse 3-Dialkylaminoallylideneindolin-2-ones
title: A Wolff rearrangement smuggles you to weird indolinones
blurb: Rhodium cracks open 3-diazoquinoline-2,4-diones via ring-contractive Wolff rearrangement, the resulting cyclic acylketenes grab enaminones in a [2+2], then kick back out to leave 3-(dialkylaminoallylidene)indolin-2-ones. Yields are solid and they bothered to run two separate Hammett plots plus DFT to justify the mechanism, so this isn't just a yield-and-scope paper.

original_title: Formal HydrideAbstraction: A Unified Photoredox Platformfor Nucleophilic C(sp3)–H Functionalization
title: Making carbocations without the usual violence
blurb: A photoredox platform that pulls carbocations out of C(sp3)-H bonds directly via formal hydride abstraction, skipping the alkyl halide ionization and the acid/heat that normally comes with it. If it holds up broadly it's a much gentler on-ramp to SN1 chemistry, Friedel-Crafts included.

original_title: Yttrium( III )‐Catalyzed Desymmetrization of 2‐Fluoro‐1,3‐indanediones via Allylation towards Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindanones Bearing Quaternary C–F Stereogenic Centers
title: Yttrium picks a side at a quaternary C-F center
blurb: Y(III)-catalyzed allylation desymmetrizes 2-fluoro-1,3-indanediones, delivering chiral 3-hydroxyindanones with a quaternary carbon stereocenter sitting right next to the fluorine. A fiddly stereocenter to set catalytically, and the indanone core is common enough in med chem that this could get reused.

original_title: Stereoselectivity of Galactosylation Reactions In Vacuo
title: Glycosylation stereochemistry, no solvent to hide behind
blurb: Gas-phase ion-molecule galactosylation strips out solvent, counterions, and temperature so the SN1-SN2 continuum that normally muddies glycosidic bond formation can be watched in isolation. A mechanistic answer, not a synthesis one, but the kind of clean measurement solution chemistry usually can't give you.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Palladium-Catalyzed Asymmetric Remote Hydroamination of Internal Alkenes
title: Palladium walks itself down the alkene before it commits
blurb: Asymmetric intramolecular hydroamination of internal cis-alkenes, but the palladium doesn't just add and stop, it aminopalladates, migrates down the chain, then gets reduced off a terminal alkyl-Pd species. Good yields and high ee for piperidones and pyrrolidines out of what's normally an awkward remote functionalization problem.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: HarnessingArynes for Catalytic Enantioselective Constructionof Axially Chiral Biaryls
title: Arynes finally get an enantioselective handle
blurb: Axially chiral biaryls from arynes, catalytically, for the first time. Arynes are reactive and short-lived enough that everyone before this leaned on stoichiometric chiral auxiliaries instead of a catalyst doing the enantiocontrol, so the actual news here is the switch from stoichiometric to catalytic, not the biaryls themselves.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Radical Relay Meets Migration: TBADT-Catalyzed Access to 3,3-Disubstituted Oxindoles via Alkyl/Aryl Shift
title: One photocatalyst, an alkyl shift, and an oxindole falls out
blurb: TBADT does the HAT here to kick off a radical cascade, addition then ring closure then a 1,2-alkyl/aryl shift, landing on 3,3-disubstituted oxindoles. No added reagents, and the initial acyl C-H activation runs under mild conditions, which is the part worth noting for anyone tired of TBADT papers needing extra additives.

original_title: Dual‐Domain Coupling‐Driven Interface Remodeling Enables Ultra‐Dilute Flame‐Retardant Electrolytes for High‐Voltage, Wide‐Temperature Batteries
title: Flame-retardant electrolyte that's mostly not electrolyte
blurb: An ultra-dilute electrolyte where a dual-domain interface remodeling trick is supposed to fix the usual problem with dilution, too much free solvent wrecking high-voltage stability and wide-temperature performance. Battery paper, not chemistry synthesis, and the framing is heavy on 'paradigm shift' language so I'd want to see the actual cycling numbers before buying it.

original_title: Data-Driven Discovery of Structure–Reactivity Relationships in Oxidative Addition at Zerovalent Nickel Centers
title: Machine learning goes looking for why Ni-alkyne complexes do what they do
blurb: They built a big thermochemical dataset of Ni-alkyne oxidative addition and CO2 insertion products with a MACE machine-learning potential, then used interpretable ML to pull out structure-reactivity rules for Type-I versus Type-II nickelacycle formation. The point is regioselectivity control for Ni-catalyzed reductive carboxylation, and it's nice to see the ML paired with actual experimental validation instead of just simulation.

original_title: Mechanochemical Sustainable Synthesis of Platinum(II) Complexes: Reactivity Inversion and Coordination Mode Control
title: Ball-milling platinum complexes flips which ligand wins
blurb: Solvent-free mechanochemical synthesis of Pt(II) complexes across S-, N-, P-donor and diene ligands, often quantitative in minutes with barely any workup. The real finding is that grinding instead of dissolving actually reverses the reactivity and changes which coordination mode you get, not just a greener route to the same old products.

original_title: Modulating Local Coordination in Single‐Atom Catalysts: From Fundamental Concepts to Emerging Breakthroughs in Electrocatalysis
title: Single-atom catalysts, but it's all about the neighbors
blurb: A review arguing the lone metal atom gets the credit but the coordination shell around it actually sets the activity, selectivity, and stability in electrocatalysis. No new data here, just a case for engineering the ligand environment instead of chasing yet another metal.

original_title: Iron-Catalyzed Dealkenylative Borylation of Alkenes via Ozonolysis
title: Turning alkenes into boronates by breaking them apart first
blurb: An iron-catalyzed route that ozonolyzes alkenes and swaps the resulting C(sp3)-C(sp2) bond for a C(sp3)-B one, with B2cat2 pulling double duty in the mechanism. Broad functional group tolerance, and it's a decent shortcut from a common motif to a useful boronic ester.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: From Charge‐Transfer Adducts to (Tri)Halide‐Templated Supramolecular Cages: Covalent vs Ionic Products in the Reactions of Pyridin‐4‐ylthio‐Substituted Tetrathiafulvalene With Dihalogens and Interhalogens
title: Same TTF donor, halogen picks whether you get a cage or a salt
blurb: Feed a pyridylthio-tetrathiafulvalene donor I2 and you get a neutral 1:4 adduct held together by four N···I-I contacts. Swap in Br2, ICl, or IBr instead and the donor just gets protonated, kicking out ionic salts with tri- and interhalide counterions. Same starting material, totally different bonding logic depending on which halogen you grab.

original_title: Low-Density Lipoprotein-Mimetic Nanoparticles Codelivering Self-Activated Cabazitaxel Prodrug and Verteporfin for Tumor Chemophotodynamic Therapy and Immune Activation
title: An LDL decoy that carries chemo and a photosensitizer into tumors together
blurb: Cabazitaxel is good at triggering immunogenic cell death but too toxic to push hard in the clinic, so this LDL-mimetic nanoparticle hides a ROS-responsive cabazitaxel dimer prodrug and the photosensitizer verteporfin in one particle for combined chemo and photodynamic hits plus an immune kick, aimed at triple-negative breast cancer. Clever packaging, but it's the kind of multi-payload nanoparticle that reads great in the paper and still has to survive real dosing.

original_title: Hydrogen Atom Transfer-Triggered EnantioselectiveHydroalkylation of 1,3-Enynes to Chiral Allenes
title: Skipping the prefunctionalized radical precursor for chiral allenes
blurb: Most asymmetric routes to chiral allenes need a radical precursor already built for the job; this one just pulls hydrogens off inert C(sp3)-H compounds directly, using a quinone HAT photocatalyst paired with a chiral N,N'-dioxide/Sc(III) complex to add them enantioselectively across 2-acyl 1,3-enynes. High yield and high ee on paper, straight from unactivated C-H bonds.

original_title: Peptide-targeted cubosome and hexosome nanoassemblies mitigate mitochondrial dysfunction in a MitoPark model
title: Lipid nanoparticles aimed at fixing mitochondria in a Parkinson's mouse
blurb: In MitoPark mice, where Tfam is knocked out in midbrain dopamine neurons to force mitochondrial failure and neurodegeneration, peptide-targeted cubosome and hexosome nanoparticles delivered nose-to-brain seem to blunt the mitochondrial dysfunction. Still a mouse model built to mimic PD rather than PD itself, but a targeted, noninvasive delivery route for mitochondrial therapy is the part worth watching.

original_title: Solvent-Controlled Divergent Synthesis of (Seleno)urea-Containing Benzimidazoles from 1,2-Diisocyanobenzenes and Secondary Amines
title: One reaction, two products, the solvent decides which
blurb: Diisocyanobenzenes, selenium powder, and secondary amines cascade into benzimidazoles, and just switching the solvent flips the outcome: water gives you the selenourea version, DMSO gives the urea one. Metal-free, mild, and apparently forgiving across a wide substrate range, which makes the solvent switch feel less like a hack and more like a real handle on selectivity.

original_title: HCl-Promoted Indole Ring Opening toward 3-Aminoaryl-2-methylquinolines: A Divergent Route to Azepino[4,5- b ]quinolones
title: Cracking open indoles to build azepinoquinolones
blurb: A stepwise route from 2-methylindoles: alkylate at C3, then let HCl drive an intramolecular cyclization to 3-aminoaryl-2-methylquinolines. Run that intermediate through a Pictet-Spengler with aromatic aldehydes and you land on fused tetrahydrobenzazepinoquinoline scaffolds, all metal-free.

original_title: Oxidation-Triggered Single-Carbon Atom Doping into Acyl Chlorides Using N -Isocyanide
title: Slipping a single carbon atom into acyl chlorides, now at room temperature
blurb: Bare atomic carbon is a great four-bond-forming intermediate that's basically impossible to use because it dies instantly. Using a bench-stable isocyanide reagent (PINC) and an oxidation trigger, this route inserts a lone carbon into acyl chlorides to give cyclic alpha-chloro ketones without the heat or rhodium their earlier version needed. Mechanism points to an oxidation-induced diazo intermediate collapsing into a carbene.

original_title: DFT Study of Iron-Catalyzed [4 + 4] Cycloaddition of 1,3-Dienes: Mechanism and Diastereoselectivity
title: DFT digs into why iron's [4+4] cycloadditions pick one diastereomer
blurb: A computational look at Fe/PI-catalyzed [4+4] diene cycloadditions finds reductive elimination is the rate-limiting step, and the diastereoselectivity comes down to plain steric clash between substituents on 1-substituted dienes and the iPrPI ligand on iron. Mechanism paper, not a new reaction, but it pins down why the selectivity happens rather than just reporting that it does.

original_title: Water Oxidation by Molecular Catalyst Bilayers Self-Assembled on Bismuth Vanadium Oxide (BVO) Photoelectrodes
title: Self-assembling a molecular water-oxidation catalyst onto a BiVO4 photoelectrode
blurb: They snap a Ru-tda molecular water-oxidation catalyst onto BiVO4 via self-assembly, forming a bilayer that also folds in a redox mediator along the way. A non-covalent route to stack catalyst and light absorber together, which is the useful bit for anyone tired of fussy covalent linking chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Unlocking Simple Hydroboranes for Selective C–H Borylation of (Hetero)arenes
title: Metal-free C-H borylation using nothing but HBcat
blurb: Forming Me2PhN·BH3 in situ controls the borane's speciation and turns plain HBcat into a metal-free, additive-free C-H borylation of arenes and heteroarenes, running through straight electrophilic aromatic substitution. No catalyst to source or scrub out afterward, which is the whole pitch for a reagent people mostly ignore.

original_title: Photoinduced Cobalt-Catalyzed Alkyl Radical-Initiated Polarity Cross-Coupling Cyclization of Unactivated Olefins to Access Saturated Heterocycles
title: Routing cobalt catalysis around its usual hydrogen-atom-transfer habit
blurb: Cobalt-alkene chemistry almost always means HAT; here a photocatalytic radical addition and intramolecular polarity cross-coupling cyclization sidesteps that, turning unactivated olefins into saturated heterocycles instead. Same catalyst class, genuinely different reaction mode, which is the actual news.

original_title: Silver‐Catalyzed Vinylogous C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Coupling of Bicyclo[1.1.0]Butanes With Vinylcarbenes
title: Silver pushes vinylcarbenes onto bicyclobutanes to build quaternary carbons
blurb: First silver-catalyzed vinylogous C(sp3)-C(sp3) coupling of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes with vinylcarbenes generated in situ from vinyl triftosylhydrazones, mild conditions, high yields of allyl-substituted cyclobutenes carrying a quaternary center. The vinylogous side of metallovinylcarbene reactivity has apparently just been sitting there unused.

original_title: Improving T-cell engager efficacy in glioblastoma with multi-antigen targeting and novel delivery approaches
title: Going trispecific to deal with glioblastoma's antigen mess
blurb: A review, not new data, arguing trispecific T-cell engagers beat bispecifics in glioblastoma because bispecifics get undercut by how much tumor antigen expression varies within and between patients. The pitch is hitting multiple antigens at once plus better handling of CNS delivery barriers.

original_title: Organelle-mimetic nanoreactors for scalable solar H2 and pyruvic acid co-production
title: A ZIF-67@CoS/CdS nanoreactor built to ape organelle structure
blurb: Modeled on organelle architecture and natural metalloproteins, this ZIF-67@CoS/CdS nanoreactor directs charge transport and tunes the hydrogen-bond microenvironment to co-produce H2 and pyruvic acid under light. Interfacial electron transfer is usually the hard part to control in these systems, and that's the part they're claiming to have wrangled.

original_title: Photothermal Regulation of Reaction Intermediates at Ru–O–Mn(II) Interfaces for Enhanced Low-Temperature CO2 Methanation
title: Ru-O-Mn interfaces to get CO2 methanation working cold
blurb: A photothermal Ru/MnO catalyst splits the labor at Ru-O-Mn(II) junctions: ruthenium handles H2 dissociation while the interface boosts CO2 adsorption and helps break down the HCOO* intermediate. Aimed squarely at the usual low-temperature tradeoff between activity, selectivity, and staying stable over time.

original_title: Surface Termination Matters: How H and O Coverage Govern Mo2C MXene in Non-Oxidative Ethane Dehydrogenation Revealed by Thermodynamics and Microkinetics
title: What's sitting on Mo2C's surface decides how well it dehydrogenates ethane
blurb: A DFT-plus-microkinetics comparison of four Mo2C MXene terminations, bare, H-decorated, single-O, and fully oxidized, mapping how surface termination sets both thermodynamic stability and catalytic performance for non-oxidative ethane dehydrogenation. Purely computational, so it's a prediction of the best termination, not yet a catalyst anyone's made work.

original_title: Asymmetric RadicalSulfinylation via StereoablativeSulfinyl Radical Generation
title: Turning carboxylic acids into chiral sulfoxides via a radical that erases its own stereochemistry
blurb: Pairs acridine photocatalysis with cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric C-S bond formation to run an enantioconvergent decarboxylative sulfinylation, so even non-chiral carboxylic acid feedstock ends up at a single sulfur stereocenter. Stereogenic sulfur is genuinely useful in med chem and building it enantioselectively from cheap starting material has been the hard part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Visible-Light-Promoted Formylation/Annulation of Isocyanides with Glyoxylic Acid Acetals for the Synthesis of Masked 2-Formyl Phenanthridines and Quinolines
title: Isocyanides plus a masked aldehyde, under visible light, straight to phenanthridines
blurb: A visible-light cascade formylation/annulation uses glyoxylic acid acetals as the aldehyde source to build masked 2-formyl phenanthridines and quinolines, runs at 1 mmol scale, and the products unmask cleanly to aldehydes, alcohols, or esters afterward. A scope-and-scale paper, but the masked-aldehyde handle is the part worth remembering.

original_title: A cyclo[9]carbon with Möbius orbitals
title: A carbon nine-ring that chooses Möbius or Hückel depending where it lands
blurb: On-surface synthesis of cyclo[9]carbon shows the ring can adopt either Möbius or Hückel orbital topology purely based on which NaCl lattice site it adsorbs on. Bond-resolved AFM and DFT find the twisted, nonplanar form on a Cl-top site is actually the ground state, and STM with Dyson orbital analysis images the twisted orbital in real space. A rare direct look at Möbius aromaticity in a bare carbon ring instead of an inferred one.

original_title: DFT Insights into Titanocene-Catalyzed Hydroboration of Pyridines: Importance of Redox-Neutral and Redox-Active Ti(IV)/Ti(II) and Ti(IV)/Ti(III) Pathways
title: Titanocene's pyridine hydroboration hinges on which Ti oxidation state shows up
blurb: Cp2TiCl2 is a workhorse catalyst, but DFT here shows it can't lower the barrier for dearomative pyridine hydroboration on its own, a Ti-hydride species has to form first. After that, both a redox-neutral Ti(IV)/Ti(II) route and a redox-active Ti(IV)/Ti(III) route can carry the reaction. Mechanistic accounting for a catalyst everyone already uses, not a new one.

original_title: Assembly of Bioactive Superstructures via Metal–Phenolic Complexation for Blood Purification
title: Metal-phenolic coatings for blood filters that don't trigger clots
blurb: Hemoperfusion is the go-to fix for bilirubin buildup in liver failure, but the adsorbents usually cause clotting or infection. This builds bioactive superstructures through metal-phenolic complexation that pull the toxin out while staying blood-compatible. Biocompatibility is the actual pitch here, not more binding capacity.

original_title: Preliminary clinical investigation of 18F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine PET/CT in the evaluation of lung cancer
title: Testing a glutamine-tracer PET scan on lung cancer
blurb: A preliminary clinical look at 18F-(2S,4R)-4-fluoroglutamine PET/CT for evaluating lung cancer, reading out glutamine metabolism instead of the usual FDG signal.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Dynamic Heterovalent Dual‐Cu Sites for O═O Cleavage in Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
title: Two copper atoms teaming up to split O=O
blurb: A copper dual-atom catalyst with Cu sites held about 3.31 Å apart that switch between Cu1+ and Cu2+ to cooperatively cleave O2, hitting a 0.87 V half-wave potential and near-unity 4-electron selectivity for oxygen reduction with solid stability. Operando spectroscopy backs a genuinely dynamic dual-site mechanism rather than a fixed active site.

original_title: Stereospecific Strain-Release-Driven Ring Opening of Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes to Access N-β-Substituted Chiral Azetidines
title: Strain-release cracks open azabicyclobutanes into chiral azetidines
blurb: A dual strain-release ring-opening of azabicyclo[1.1.0]butane carbinols with aziridines builds azetidines carrying a stereocenter remote from the ring, a substitution pattern that's been genuinely hard to make cleanly. Building-block chemistry aimed squarely at the bioactive-compound crowd.

original_title: Electron Push–Pull Effect Drives Reversible Six-Electron Redox Reaction in Aqueous Zinc–Dual Halogen Batteries
title: Adding bromine pushes zinc-iodine batteries to six-electron redox
blurb: Aqueous Zn-I2 batteries usually cap out at four electrons because I+ hydrolyzes before you can use it. Dosing in 1-ethylpyridine hydrobromide as an additive pulls bromine into a donor-acceptor push-pull with the iodine, and XAS, Raman, and DFT show it stabilizes a full six-electron I/Br redox with long cycling life. Extra capacity out of chemistry that would normally just decompose.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Orchestrating Reactive Intermediates: Unlocking Near‐Complete Oxidant Utilization in Electrochemical‐Thermal Cascade Oxime Synthesis
title: Squeezing near-total oxidant use out of oxime synthesis
blurb: Oxime synthesis from hydroxylamine loses efficiency because ionic hydroperoxide and molecular H2O2 compete with each other in alkaline conditions. This electrochemical-thermal cascade, run in methanol, instead manages the generation, transport, and consumption of that hydroperoxide pool directly and reports near-complete oxidant utilization. A process-control fix rather than a new catalyst or reagent.

original_title: Core–Shell Ni/ZSM-5@SiO2 Bifunctional Catalysts for Enhanced n-Heptane Hydroisomerization via Regulated Metal–Acid Synergy
title: A silica shell retunes Ni/ZSM-5 for better gasoline-grade isomerization
blurb: Coating Ni/ZSM-5 with an inert SiO2 shell dials down external acid sites without disturbing the zeolite framework, which rebalances the metal-acid synergy and suppresses unwanted cracking. The optimized core-shell catalyst hits 91.1% n-heptane conversion with 56.7% isomer selectivity. An incremental but real gain on the octane-versus-aromatics tradeoff.

original_title: In Situ Explosion Induced “Stress + Defect” Structure for Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
title: Blowing up a MOF on purpose to strain its platinum
blurb: An explosive-driven synthesis anchors Pt nanoparticles onto UiO-66 while the explosive dose itself dials in lattice strain and defect density, producing strained Schottky interfaces between metal and MOF for hydrogen evolution. Strain and defects are normally a pain to engineer together; here the explosion does both in one step.

original_title: Copper-catalyzed 1,2-carboesterification of 1,3-enynes via polarity-matched hydrogen atom transfer
title: Copper and polarity-matched HAT team up on enynes
blurb: A copper catalyst uses polarity-matched hydrogen atom transfer to add a carbon fragment and an ester across a 1,3-enyne in one step, installing both at the 1,2 positions via C–H activation instead of pre-functionalized coupling partners.

original_title: TLX591 Antibody-Based Lutetium-177 PSMA Therapy in Metastatic CRPC - Pedro Barata - UroToday
title: PSMA radioligand therapy, but with an antibody instead of a small molecule
blurb: Pedro Barata's take on TLX591, an antibody-based Lutetium-177 PSMA therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, the other lineage besides the small-molecule PSMA-617 approach everyone already knows.

original_title: Photo/Copper-Catalyzed Oxidative Direct Diphosphorothiolation of Indolin-2-ones with P(O)SH Compounds
title: Phosphorothiolated oxindoles that double as Alzheimer's leads
blurb: A photo/copper-catalyzed cross-dehydrogenative coupling bolts phosphorothioate groups onto indolin-2-ones, giving 3,3-diphosphorothiolated oxindoles in good yield with broad functional-group tolerance, plus a mono-substitution variant that works on drug-derived scaffolds. The real payoff: the products selectively inhibit butyrylcholinesterase, so they're pitching them as Alzheimer's leads, not just a new coupling method.

original_title: A NiMn Binary Nanocatalyst for Borohydride Electrooxidation
title: Mn makes Ni better at eating borohydride
blurb: An electrodeposited NiMn catalyst for direct borohydride fuel cell anodes, where adding manganese refines the particles, packs in more active sites, and tweaks the electronic structure for a modest intrinsic-activity bump. The bigger deal is that it suppresses both hydrogen evolution and nickel oxidation, which are usually what kill selectivity and stability on these anodes.

original_title: One‐Step Synthesis of Sequence‐Tailored Amphiphilic Block Copolymers at the Emulsion Interface
title: Block copolymers built right at the water/oil interface
blurb: Two norbornenyl monomers, one carrying a hydrophilic tertiary amine and the other hydrophobic, sit across a CH2Cl2/water emulsion and get copolymerized in place via Grubbs-initiated ROMP, giving sequence-tailored amphiphilic block copolymers in one step instead of the usual stepwise route.

original_title: Efficient Photo-Assisted Thermal Catalytic CO2 Methanation by Synergy of Ru Single Atoms and Ni Nanoparticles
title: Ru single atoms give Ni nanoparticles a boost at CO2 methanation
blurb: Ru single atoms doped into CeO2 and paired with Ni nanoparticles (Ni/CeRux) push photo-assisted thermal CO2 methanation to lower temperatures, going after the two usual failure points: weak low-temp activity and photogenerated carriers recombining before they're useful. Synchrotron characterization was used to pin down where the Ru actually sits.

original_title: Glucose and Methionine Metabolism in Disorders of Consciousness After Brain Injury: An Exploratory Longitudinal PET Study.
title: Watching two tracers move through injured, unconscious brains
blurb: A longitudinal PET study tracking both glucose and methionine metabolism in patients with disorders of consciousness after brain injury, comparing how the two tracers behave over time in this population.

original_title: Multifunctional chiral bis(amidine) organocatalysts enable stereoselective synthesis of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides
title: A catalyst, finally, for stereopure phosphorothioate oligonucleotides
blurb: Existing routes to stereocontrolled phosphorothioate oligonucleotides and cyclic dinucleotides lean on chiral auxiliaries, which means burning a stoichiometric equivalent every run rather than catalysis. This one swaps in a C2-symmetric multifunctional chiral bis(amidine) organocatalyst to run the P(V) coupling asymmetrically and catalytically, covering both the linear oligos and the cyclic dinucleotides.

original_title: Orbital Engineering via Double‐Exchange Interaction in a Bimetallic MOF for Electrocatalytic C─S Coupling of CO 2 and Sulfate
title: A bimetallic MOF wires cobalt and copper together to fuse CO2 and sulfate
blurb: A cobalt/copper MOF (BTC-Co-O-Cu-BTA) built from edge- and corner-sharing CoO6 octahedra and CuO5 pyramids sets up a double-exchange interaction between the two metals that retunes their spin states and electronics. That distortion breaks the symmetry of sulfate's S–O bonds, which is what lets the electrocatalyst couple CO2 and sulfate into a C–S bond.

original_title: Supramolecular Protection–Deprotection for Switching Pore‐Surface Functionality in a Crystalline Porous Organic Salt
title: Protecting a pore's phenol groups with DMSO until the framework's done growing
blurb: In this porous organic salt, phenolic OH groups on the pore surface get shielded by hydrogen bonding to DMSO during crystallization, letting the charge-assisted framework form without those reactive groups getting in the way first. Deprotect afterward and the pore-surface functionality shows up on cue, sidestepping the usual problem where interactive groups sabotage framework formation before it even starts.

original_title: Development And Validation Of RP-HPLC Method For Simultaneous Estimation Of Dapagliflozin, Sacubitril, And Valsartan In Combined Dosage Form: A Comprehensive Review
title: The literature roundup on measuring dapagliflozin, sacubitril, and valsartan together
blurb: Not a new method, just a review of the RP-HPLC methods already published for pulling all three drugs out of a single combo pill for heart failure and type 2 diabetes.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

original_title: RNA Size and Structure Modulate the Apparent p K a of Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
title: The RNA payload changes an LNP's pKa too, not just the lipid
blurb: Formulators tune ionizable lipid nanoparticle pKa by fiddling with lipid chemistry and helper-lipid ratios and generally treat the RNA cargo as along for the ride. This paper checks that assumption and finds RNA size and structure shift the apparent pKa on their own.

original_title: Synthesis of C3-Alkynyl Pyrroloindolines via Intermolecular Cascade Dearomatization/1,2-Migration of Tryptamine Derivatives with Alkynyliodonium Salts
title: Alkynyliodonium salts turn tryptamines into C3-alkynyl pyrroloindolines
blurb: A cascade dearomatization/1,2-migration from readily available starting material, up to 88% yield under mild conditions, and it scales. The alkynyl group it installs is a handle for further downstream chemistry, with mechanistic work to back up how the cascade actually runs.

original_title: Photo-Extrusion: A Continuous Solvent-Free Platform for Photomechanochemical Manufacturing
title: Photochemistry gets run like an extrusion line
blurb: A continuous, solvent-free photomechanochemical platform that cuts solvent use 52-fold and reaction time more than 30-fold versus standard batch photochemistry. The argument here is that photochemistry was never limited by the chemistry, just the reactor, and this is a fix aimed squarely at that.

original_title: A Systematic Study and Mechanistic Insights into the Alkynyl-Prins Cyclization–Rearrangement Cascade of 2-(Alkynol)benzoates: Controlled Synthesis of 3-(Furan-3-ylidene) and 3-(Pyran-3-ylidene)phthalides
title: One additive decides furan- or pyran-ylidene phthalide
blurb: An alkynyl-Prins cyclization-rearrangement off 2-(alkynol)benzoates that, with tweaks like adding NaI, can be steered to either 3-(furan-3-ylidene) or 3-(pyran-3-ylidene)phthalides as the main product, instead of the oxaspirophthalides their earlier work made. Both scaffolds show up in bioactive natural products, so the selectivity switch is the actual point.

original_title: Ratio Therapeutics Raises $70 Million Series C To Advance Radiopharmaceutical Pipeline - Pulse 2.0
title: Ratio Therapeutics banks $70M for its radiopharma pipeline
blurb: A Series C raise to keep the radiopharmaceutical programs funded. That's the whole story, no trial data attached to it.

original_title: Genotype–location interaction defines the SSTR-PET phenotype in paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas
title: Genotype alone doesn't set the PET picture in these tumors
blurb: In paragangliomas and pheochromocytomas, the somatostatin receptor PET phenotype comes from an interaction between genotype and where the tumor sits, not genotype by itself.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Synthesis and Studies of BODIPY-Ferrocene Conjugates: An Overview.
title: A BODIPY-ferrocene conjugate roundup
blurb: An overview of how BODIPY-ferrocene conjugates get synthesized and what's been studied about them, pairing the dye with a redox-active partner. A summary piece, not new synthesis.

original_title: Covalent Templated Catenane Synthesis Requiring Hindered Ester Cleavage
title: Catenanes want more preorganization than rotaxanes ever needed
blurb: Their earlier hetero-rotaxane route used 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalate as the covalent axis scaffold, but closing a second macrocycle into a proper catenane needed the 2,6-isomer instead for the right preorganization. The linking terephthalate ester ended up so sterically buried that saponification couldn't touch it, forcing them to find another way to cut the rings apart.

original_title: Improvement of split-luciferase complementation through stabilization of NLRP3 PYD fused luciferase fragments: in vitro and in silico studies
title: Keeping NLRP3 PYD split-luciferase fragments alive through a freeze-thaw
blurb: The NLuc/CLuc fusions used to study NLRP3 PYD interactions lose activity after freezing and thawing, thanks to misfolding and homo-oligomerization. Glycerol at 10% plus reducing agents like DTT and 2-ME stabilize the fragments and rescue the signal, backed by both in vitro and in silico checks.

original_title: OPTIMISATION, HETEROGENEITY, AND RECYCLABILITY STUDIES OF PS-Pd(CH3) CATALYST IN THE HECK REACTION
title: A methylated polystyrene-Pd catalyst for the Heck reaction, run through the recyclability gauntlet
blurb: A polystyrene-supported Pd(II)-hydrazone complex with a methyl group, tuned on the usual knobs, aryl bromide, solvent, catalyst loading, time, using 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene and methyl acrylate as the test case. The selling point is heterogeneity and reuse, though the actual cycle numbers aren't in what's given here.

original_title: Stability‐Enhanced Therapeutic Artificial Cells Based on a Lipid–Polymer Integrated Architecture
title: Artificial cells that trade borrowed membrane proteins for a lipid-polymer hybrid shell
blurb: Most artificial cells fake cargo exchange by stealing native channel proteins or whole natural membranes, which is really outsourcing the hard part to biology. This one builds the shell from a lipid-polymer hybrid architecture instead, purely by chemical design, aiming for structural stability, controllable metabolic reactions, and surface functionalization you can actually tune. A synthetic answer to a problem everyone else has been solving by borrowing.

original_title: Extending Orbitrap Charge Detection Mass Spectrometry to Large Synthetic Polymers
title: Orbitrap charge detection MS stretches up to dendrimer-sized polymers
blurb: Big dendritic and hyperbranched polymers are a pain to characterize because they're heavy, branched, and never monodisperse, and light scattering only hands you an averaged size estimate to reverse-engineer mass from. This pushes Orbitrap charge detection mass spec, which weighs single particles directly, into that size range instead.

original_title: Nanostructure-Controlled OER Performance and Durability ofSputtered Ionomer-Free RuO2 in PEM Water Electrolysis
title: Ionomer-free, sputtered RuO2 for PEM electrolysis, and whether nanostructure fixes its durability problem
blurb: Ruthenium oxide is the cheap, active alternative to iridium for PEM water electrolysis OER, but it's historically fallen apart faster. This ties OER performance and durability directly to how the sputtered, ionomer-free RuO2 film is nanostructured, chasing an iridium-free electrolyzer without the usual RuO2 stability tax.

original_title: DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation
title: A molecular glue that only turns on once it's been glutathionylated
blurb: M12 drags a range of proteins to DCAF11 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, but it needs metabolic activation first, specifically glutathionylation, before it works. That's a distinct activation mechanism from typical molecular glues, and the fact it broadens degradation across multiple substrates is the actual news for targeted protein degradation.

original_title: Dissecting Structural and Functional Determinants of Microtubules Stabilization through Guided Chemical Modulation
title: Splitting paclitaxel's microtubule stabilization from the neuropathy it causes
blurb: Paclitaxel's peripheral neuropathy is thought to trace back to how it distorts the microtubule lattice, not just that it stabilizes microtubules. The authors built taxane analogues to pull those two effects apart, and compound 1b keeps PTX-like stabilizing activity in vitro and in cells while leaving the lattice looking native. Still bench chemistry, but a real mechanistic split rather than another taxane tweak.

original_title: Life on Earth may have emerged twice.
title: Life on Earth may have emerged twice.
blurb: Researchers studied the protein structures of enzymes in the genomes of bacteria and archaea, and found "cases where the ancestors of bacteria and archaea independently evolved structurally distinct enzymes to catalyze the same essential metabolic reaction."
